candidate_relationships.title: Genetic relatedness repeatedly structures burial membership, but the social meaning is not uniquely ancestor cult
observed_recurrences: At Ajvide/Gotland Pitted Ware co-burials, all co-buried sampled individuals were close genetic relatives extending beyond first degree.
In Neolithic Caithness and Orkney chambered tombs, many biologically male individuals in the same or nearby tombs were paternally related; architecture differed locally.

independence_checks.source_independence: Distinct research teams, sites, subsistence contexts and burial forms; both use ancient DNA, so method family is shared but samples are independent.
independence_checks.temporal_direction: No single diffusion direction inferred. Scottish tombs c. 3800–3200 BCE; Ajvide PWC is later and in a different regional tradition. Dates establish context only.
independence_checks.geographic_contact: Both northern Europe, but direct contact pathway between the focal burial systems is not established here.
independence_checks.ancestry: Genetic relatedness is the measured within-context variable; it must not be transformed into shared-cultural ancestry between contexts.
independence_checks.ecological_convergence: Sedentism/subsistence, cemetery organization and local demography could independently favor kin-clustered burial.
independence_checks.coding_translation: Biological relatedness, social kinship, descent, affinity, burial membership and ancestor worship are separate variables.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Burial groups materially encode socially salient descent/kin relations.
rival_hypotheses.support: Consistent with both datasets; stronger in the Scottish patrilineal pattern.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Kin clustering emerges pragmatically from household/local cemetery use without explicit descent ideology.
rival_hypotheses.support: Compatible with localized burial access and demography.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Broader social kin or affiliation, only partly biological, governs inclusion.
rival_hypotheses.support: Cummings explicitly distinguishes social kinship from biological relatedness.
rival_hypotheses.risk: Hard to recover without isotopes/material networks/text.

candidate_relationships.null_explanation: Burial membership is no more associated with close genetic relatedness than expected from local population structure, cemetery sampling and household spatial autocorrelation.
falsification_criteria: Matched cemeteries with adequate genomic coverage show no excess relatedness among co-burials after local population structure is modeled.
Tomb/cemetery membership predicts unrelated social affiliates better than genetic kin across multiple independent contexts.
discriminating_evidence: Multi-site ancient-DNA datasets with contemporaneous background-population controls.
Isotope mobility, residence patterns, sex-biased mobility and settlement-household linkage.
Explicit model comparing kin selection, spatial proximity and burial architecture.

candidate_relationships.title: Ritual environments may repeatedly use controllable sensory intensity as an altered-experience technology
observed_recurrences: Measured Etruscan tomb acoustics show strong differences in reverberation and spatial affordances; trance-like interpretation is an author-level inference.
Independent neurobiological work associates repetitive rhythmic sound with altered-state reports and distinct brain/network changes.
Immersive context can change mystical-type reports even with matched content, supporting context as a separable induction variable.

independence_checks.source_independence: Archaeological acoustics, laboratory/neurophysiology and immersive-context studies are methodologically independent.
independence_checks.temporal_direction: Modern mechanism studies cannot date or prove ancient intention; they only establish plausible affordance mechanisms.
independence_checks.geographic_contact: No cross-cultural diffusion is required for the physiological mechanism candidate.
independence_checks.ancestry: Shared human sensory/neural constraints are a convergence alternative, not evidence of shared ritual ancestry.
independence_checks.ecological_convergence: Enclosed spaces naturally create acoustic effects; intentional exploitation must be demonstrated against architectural nulls.
independence_checks.coding_translation: Altered state, trance, fear, absorption, mystical-type report and ritual efficacy are not interchangeable.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Architectural/sound design was intentionally selected to modulate attention, arousal or absorption.
rival_hypotheses.support: Plausible where acoustic effects align with movement/iconography.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Sensory effects are architectural by-products later incorporated into ritual.
Modern participants/researchers project altered-state categories onto spaces whose ritual function was different.
rival_hypotheses.risk: Can be reduced by emic texts/iconography where available.

candidate_relationships.null_explanation: Measured acoustic/visual properties do not exceed what comparable non-ritual structures produce and have no reproducible effect on perception beyond generic enclosure/context effects.
falsification_criteria: Matched architectural controls eliminate the sensory differences.
Blind experimental reconstructions show no effect of the distinctive acoustic features on arousal/absorption once expectation is controlled.
discriminating_evidence: Pre-registered acoustic comparison across ritual and non-ritual structures.
Blind/VR reconstructions separating geometry, sound, darkness, iconography and expectation.
Direct archaeological indicators of music, movement, lighting or repeated ritual positioning.

candidate_relationships.title: Synchrony plus arousal is a plausible recurrent mechanism linking collective ritual participation to short-run cohesion/cooperation
observed_recurrences: A field experiment manipulating synchrony and physiological arousal found effects on clustering and cooperation.
A naturalistic ancestor festival study found associations between active participation/ancestral belief and several cohesion/prosocial outcomes.

independence_checks.source_independence: Experimental strangers and a naturally occurring Japanese ritual are independent designs and populations.
independence_checks.temporal_direction: Experimental manipulation supports short-run causal direction for synchrony/arousal; naturalistic belief-participation associations remain correlational.
independence_checks.geographic_contact: No historical connection is needed for the mechanism; do not infer common origin of rituals.
independence_checks.ancestry: Shared psychology is an explicit convergence hypothesis.
independence_checks.ecological_convergence: Group-size, threat, costly participation and local institutions can moderate or generate the association.
independence_checks.coding_translation: Cohesion, cooperation, generosity, identity and doctrinal belief are separate outcomes.

rival_hypotheses.risk: External validity across ritual forms varies.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Pre-existing group commitment selects people into active ritual roles.
Shared attention and common goals, not synchrony specifically, drive bonding.

candidate_relationships.null_explanation: After controlling shared goals, expectation, prior commitment and arousal, synchrony contributes no additional cohesion/cooperation.
falsification_criteria: Factorial replications across cultures show no synchrony-specific effect.
Effects disappear when experimenter demand and common-goal cues are controlled.
discriminating_evidence: Longitudinal measures separating selection into ritual from post-participation change.

candidate_relationships.title: Sacred-place norms can function as ecological protection, but reverse causation and remoteness remain serious rivals
observed_recurrences: Sacred natural sites are reported across traditions as areas governed by restrictions, taboos or ritual norms.
Some controlled local studies find higher habitat/species diversity at sacred sites than surrounding landscapes.

independence_checks.source_independence: Evidence spans multiple regions, but syntheses can reuse the same case studies; independence must be tracked at site level.
independence_checks.temporal_direction: Current biodiversity advantage does not establish whether sacredness caused protection or biodiverse/remnant sites became sacred.
independence_checks.geographic_contact: Wide geographic recurrence makes a single diffusion story unnecessary and implausible as a default.
independence_checks.ancestry: Religious labels are heterogeneous; shared ancestry must be controlled within regional clusters.
independence_checks.ecological_convergence: High: remoteness, terrain, low agricultural value and historical land-use may cause both sacred-site persistence and biodiversity.
independence_checks.coding_translation: Sacred, taboo, protected, customary governance and low-use are different constructs.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Sacred norms reduce extraction/disturbance and thereby conserve biodiversity.
rival_hypotheses.support: Mechanistically plausible and observed in some sites.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Ecologically distinctive/refugial places are preferentially sacralized.
Remoteness/topography/governance, not sacredness, explains the biodiversity difference.

candidate_relationships.null_explanation: Sacred designation has no biodiversity effect once remoteness, land-use history, habitat type and governance are matched.
falsification_criteria: Matched-pair or longitudinal analyses show no sacred-status effect.
Biodiversity differences predate known sacralization or track topography/access rather than norms.
discriminating_evidence: Historical/remote-sensing trajectories before and after changes in sacred governance.
Matched sacred/non-sacred sites within the same habitat and accessibility class.
Independent ethnographic documentation of actual extraction rules and enforcement.

candidate_relationships.title: Astronomical orientation recurs in sacred architecture, but high researcher degrees of freedom make many individual claims non-discriminating
observed_recurrences: Some monument traditions show statistically patterned solar/stellar orientations.
Other heavily claimed sites fail when tested with predefined selection criteria and pseudo-random simulations.

independence_checks.source_independence: Site studies are independent only when orientations and target definitions are not inherited from earlier claims.
independence_checks.temporal_direction: Astronomical calculations can date possible alignments but should not be used alone to date monuments or infer ritual origin.
independence_checks.geographic_contact: Similar solar/lunar alignment can arise independently anywhere due to shared sky geometry.
independence_checks.ancestry: Within-region architectural traditions require ancestry/contact controls.
independence_checks.ecological_convergence: Horizon/topography, slope, prevailing access and cardinal planning can mimic astronomical orientation.
independence_checks.coding_translation: Alignment, calendrical function, observatory, sacred significance and intentionality are separate claims.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Builders intentionally oriented monuments to recurrent celestial events for calendrical/ritual purposes.
Topography/access/cardinal constraints produce the orientation distribution.
Post-hoc target selection creates apparent astronomical hits.

candidate_relationships.null_explanation: Observed alignments are no more frequent or precise than expected under the available horizon, orientation and researcher-selection space.
falsification_criteria: Predefined target tests fail in complete monument samples.
Orientation signal vanishes after topographic/cardinal and multiple-comparison controls.
discriminating_evidence: Complete regional monument samples, not famous-site subsets.
Pre-registered celestial targets and tolerance windows.
Monte Carlo/null orientation models plus independent archaeological evidence for calendrical use.

candidate_relationships.title: Cross-hominin recurrence of deliberate non-utilitarian material modification supports component-level comparison, not a unitary 'behavioral modernity' or common symbolic origin
observed_recurrences: Neanderthal contexts include deliberate pigment use/marking and a 2025 pigment-marked non-utilitarian pebble interpreted by authors as potentially symbolic.
Homo sapiens Aurignacian ornaments show complex manufacture/use histories; 2026 traceology cautions that pigment residues can reflect production rather than symbolic coloration.
2026 conceptual work argues that 'behavioral modernity' obscures component-level behavioral overlap.

independence_checks.source_independence: Different species assignments, sites, teams and artifact classes improve observational independence; interpretive literature remains theoretically linked.
independence_checks.temporal_direction: Recurrence long after the Neanderthal–H. sapiens split cannot establish pre-split cultural inheritance.
independence_checks.geographic_contact: Some later populations had contact/admixture, but the candidate does not assume contact for every artifact recurrence.
independence_checks.ancestry: Deep shared biological ancestry is real but does not demonstrate transmission of a specific cultural convention.
independence_checks.ecological_convergence: Display, social coordination, material affordance and local innovation are viable convergence routes.
independence_checks.coding_translation: Anthropogenic mark, ornament, display, convention, information-bearing system, denotational symbol and religion must remain separate ladder levels.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Multiple Homo populations independently evolved socially salient material practices under similar cognitive/social constraints.
rival_hypotheses.risk: Independent invention is difficult to prove.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Some capacities/practice tendencies were inherited from deeper shared ancestry.
rival_hypotheses.risk: Specific cultural transmission across hundreds of millennia is unsupported.

rival_hypotheses.statement: Apparent recurrence is category inflation: heterogeneous utilitarian/aesthetic practices are coded as symbolic.
rival_hypotheses.risk: Does not explain all deliberate patterning/display evidence.

candidate_relationships.null_explanation: Once physical observations are coded without semantic labels, there is no coherent cross-hominin behavioral construct beyond generic tool/material manipulation.
falsification_criteria: Traceology/experimental studies consistently reclassify proposed display/sign artifacts as production or taphonomic residues.
Component-level recurrence disappears when identical operational definitions are applied blind across species/context.
discriminating_evidence: Blind, preregistered component coding across Neanderthal and H. sapiens assemblages.
Direct use-wear/residue/experimental discrimination of production versus display/sign use.
Secure dating and population attribution; contact/admixture models where contemporaneous.

unexplained_high_independence_recurrence.statement: Rhythmic auditory induction of absorption/nonordinary experience recurs across culturally separated practices and has laboratory/neurobiological plausibility.
unexplained_high_independence_recurrence.why_unexplained: Shared neurophysiology is a strong convergence explanation, but the distribution, ritual packaging and cultural selection of specific rhythms remain under-modeled.

unexplained_high_independence_recurrence.statement: Close genetic relatedness structures burial grouping in distinct subsistence and architectural contexts.
unexplained_high_independence_recurrence.why_unexplained: The recurrence is compatible with several social mechanisms and does not reveal whether kinship was genealogical ideology, pragmatic cemetery access, corporate identity or a mixture.

contradictions_or_pressure.finding: 2026 conceptual/methodological work strengthens the case to retire or narrow umbrella coding; component-level claims are safer.
Pigment/ornament/non-utilitarian objects do not uniquely imply semantic symbolic function.
Alignment claims are highly vulnerable to researcher target selection and incomplete monument sampling.
Measured acoustic differences are stronger evidence than reconstructed trance/cognitive-state interpretations.
Customary omen participation can coexist with skepticism; practice must not be collapsed into propositional belief.

hypotheses_revisited.reason: New material and concept work favors deliberate patterned/socially salient material forms over a blanket symbolic label.
Cross-hominin recurrence does not require pre-split cultural transmission; convergence and category inflation remain live.
Graphic and ornamental practices recur, but not as one proven connected symbolic tradition.
Daily 2026-09-01 death-omens candidate directly pressures belief/practice separation.
VR, rhythm and architectural affordance evidence jointly support separating induction medium/context from phenomenology without equating states.

summary: Six relationship candidates generated. Strongest are mortuary kinship structuring and ritual synchrony/sensory mechanisms. Astronomical alignment remains deliberately fragile. No relationship was promoted to evidence, descent, common origin or supernatural explanation.
